newsitem.title: USA: Tower Air awaits Israeli green light.
newsitem.headline: Tower Air awaits Israeli green light.

text.p: Israel is expected any day now to grant Tower Air traffic rights for a new scheduled service to Tel Aviv replacing previous charter flights, Tower managing director for Europe, Reuven Wertheim told Reuters.

Tower Air begins a four times weekly New York-Athens service on June 15. It said that when Israeli approval is received this flight would then continue on to Tel Aviv twice a week before returning to New York.
From May 1 California space broker, Mercury Air Cargo, has had an exclusive charter agreement with Tower for most of the carrier's flights worldwide.
However, Mercury will not operate the cargo space on Tower's Athens-Tel Aviv connection, Mercury Air Group Inc spokesman David Herbst, told Reuters.

Tower Air operates a fleet of 19 Boeing 747-100s and 200s, including two freighters. The B747-200 has an approximate six tonne cargo capacity. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
